title: Webflow Campaigns: What It Does, and the Price It Won't Say (2026)
description: Webflow launched Campaigns, an AI tool for on-brand landing pages and ads, on October 20, 2026. We read the product page and the pricing page side by side — here's what it does, and the one thing it won't disclose.
excerpt: Webflow's new Campaigns tool builds landing pages and ads from a brief. Every other Webflow plan shows a price. This one doesn't.
intro: Webflow launched Campaigns on October 20, 2026 — an AI tool that builds on-brand landing pages and ads from one shared brief. Every other Webflow plan lists a dollar figure on its pricing page; this one shows only "Contact sales."

body:
This is a synthesis, not a hands-on test. Webflow Campaigns is reached through a "Contact sales" button, not a signup form, so there is no free account to walk through and no screenshot to take. What follows is a direct read of Webflow's own product page, its standard pricing page, and the trade press that covered the launch — cited throughout, with nothing claimed that isn't sourced.

📋 How this was put together

Every claim below comes from Webflow's Campaigns product page, Webflow's standard pricing page, and CMSWire's launch coverage, all read on the same day in October 2026. No first-hand test of the product is claimed anywhere in this piece.

What Webflow announced on October 20

Webflow Campaigns is a standalone AI tool for demand-generation and performance marketing teams. Per CMSWire's reporting, it's built to work alongside a team's existing site — Webflow or not — rather than replace it.

The pitch: an AI agent extracts a brand's design system from the existing site, builds a shared campaign brief with the marketer, and then generates landing pages and matching ads from that one brief. Campaign types in the prompt interface include awareness, lead gen, webinar, meetup, and gated content, according to Webflow's own product page.

An Exiger marketing operations manager, quoted in the CMSWire piece, described her prior workflow as mocking pages up in Lovable and rebuilding them in WordPress — two separate tools and two separate rebuilds for one campaign. Campaigns is pitched as collapsing that into one pass, with "campaign analytics right alongside the page," in her words.

The one thing every other Webflow plan tells you that Campaigns won't

Webflow's standard pricing page is unusually transparent, as SaaS pricing pages go. Starter is free. Basic is $15 a month billed yearly. Premium is $25 a month billed yearly. The Team platform plan shows a number too — $2,500 a month, on an annual contract — even though its button reads "Talk to us" rather than "Buy now." Only the Enterprise tier, the last row on the page, drops the dollar figure in favor of "Custom."

Campaigns breaks that pattern entirely. Its own product page carries no pricing table, no plan comparison, and no number of any kind. The only call to action on the page is "Contact sales."

"Four of Webflow's five site plans show a dollar figure on the page. Campaigns, the newest product, shows none."

That's not unusual for a brand-new enterprise product — plenty of martech launches start sales-led and add self-serve pricing later. It's still worth naming plainly, because CMSWire's own launch coverage doesn't mention pricing at all, and Webflow's product page gives a reader nothing to budget against before they've already booked a call.

What it can actually do, per the product page

Setting pricing aside, the feature list on Webflow's own page is specific. Brand extraction pulls typography and color from an existing site into a reusable design system — or a marketer can supply a design.md file directly, skipping the extraction step. An AI agent then helps draft and sharpen the campaign brief itself, before any page gets built.

From that one brief, Campaigns generates landing pages and matching ad creative, plus audience-specific variations — each with its own URL and messaging, aimed at a given persona, industry, or target account. Ads come in multiple sizes and formats for the platforms a campaign runs on.

On the distribution side, pages publish to a chosen subdomain, and forms connect so conversions are tracked from first click. A built-in Google Ads integration pushes the campaign straight into a Performance Max setup, with ad copy matched to the page. HubSpot and Marketo handle forms and lead capture; HubSpot and Salesforce both get named for CRM pipeline attribution. Analytics reports on sessions, conversions, and pipeline influence, with AI-generated recommendations layered on top.

The Claude and ChatGPT detail worth noticing

One line on Webflow's product page is easy to skim past and shouldn't be: pages built in Campaigns can be edited through its own visual editor, through its built-in AI Assistant, or through the Webflow MCP — directly inside "compatible AI tools such as Claude and ChatGPT."

That's a meaningfully different build pattern than the chat-box-in-the-product approach most AI landing-page tools use. Instead of (or alongside) a prompt box built into Webflow's own interface, a marketer working from Claude or ChatGPT can reach into the same campaign through Webflow's MCP server and edit it from there. For a team already running workflows through an AI tool rather than a dozen separate browser tabs, that's the detail that would actually change how the product gets used day to day — more than the brand-extraction pitch that leads the marketing copy.

Where this fits next to Typeform, Unbounce, and Landingi

BuzzRiding has already looked at three tools chasing a version of this same job. Typeform's AI Landing Pages, launched earlier this month, bundles a page, a form, and a CRM contact into one chat-driven flow, free on every plan including its free tier. Unbounce and Landingi are dedicated page editors with AI features layered on, both with published pricing a reader can compare line by line without talking to anyone.

Webflow Campaigns sits apart from both groups on two axes. It's pitched at a different buyer — demand-gen and performance marketing teams running multi-channel campaigns with ad spend and CRM attribution attached, not a solo marketer building one page. And it's the only one of the four with no published price at all, not even a "starts at" figure to anchor expectations before a sales call.

It's also the only one of the four built around AI-tool-native editing rather than a built-in prompt box as the primary interface. Typeform, Unbounce, and Landingi all keep the AI assistant inside their own product. Webflow's MCP integration is a genuinely different architectural choice, and whether that matters to a given team depends entirely on whether that team already works inside Claude or ChatGPT for other parts of its stack.

Who should actually look at this

A demand-gen team already juggling Google Ads, a CRM, and a separate page-building tool for every campaign has a real reason to get on a call: the pitch is specifically about collapsing that coordination overhead, and the CRM and Google Ads integrations are named, not vague. A team that wants to compare cost against Unbounce or Landingi before committing any time has nothing to compare yet — that's not a knock on the product, it's a plain gap in what's published.

A solo marketer or small team building one campaign page at a time is very likely the wrong audience regardless of price. Everything about Campaigns' feature list — design-system extraction, persona-specific URL variations, CRM pipeline attribution — is built for a team running several campaigns through several channels at once, not a single landing page. That team is better served by a dedicated builder with a published price, like the one in BuzzRiding's Landingi review.

💡 Key takeaway

Webflow Campaigns launched October 20, 2026, with a specific, well-documented feature set and zero published pricing — the only one of Webflow's site plans that shows no dollar figure at all. Compare the feature list against your own campaign workflow before booking a sales call, since that call is currently the only way to learn what it costs.

The obvious caveat

This article reads Webflow's own product page, its pricing page, and one piece of launch coverage. It is not an audit and not a hands-on test, because there is no self-serve account to test. Enterprise sales conversations can land at very different price points for different company sizes and contract terms, so nothing here should stand in for an actual quote.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Webflow Campaigns?
An AI tool, launched October 20, 2026, that builds on-brand landing pages and matching ads from one shared campaign brief, with Google Ads and CRM integrations for tracking pipeline. It works alongside an existing site, whether or not that site runs on Webflow.
How much does Webflow Campaigns cost?
Webflow's product page for Campaigns lists no price; the only call to action is "Contact sales." That's different from Webflow's standard site plans, which publish dollar figures for every tier except Enterprise.
Can I use Webflow Campaigns if my website isn't built on Webflow?
Yes. Webflow's own product page describes Campaigns as working alongside any CMS, extracting brand and design context from the existing site rather than requiring a migration.
Can I edit Webflow Campaigns pages from Claude or ChatGPT?
Yes, per Webflow's product page. Pages can be edited through Campaigns' own visual editor and AI Assistant, or through the Webflow MCP server inside compatible AI tools, which the page names as including Claude and ChatGPT.
Should I pick Webflow Campaigns over Typeform, Unbounce, or Landingi?
They're not quite the same category. Typeform, Unbounce, and Landingi are built for a marketer building individual landing pages, with published pricing to compare. Campaigns targets teams running multi-channel campaigns with CRM attribution attached, and currently requires a sales conversation to learn the cost.

This post was researched and refined with AI tools.
